about: Natural State Council is a 501(c)(3) local council of Scouting America serving 67 counties across Arkansas. Formed from Quapaw Area, Westark Area, and De Soto Area councils, it supports Cub Scouts, Scouts BSA, Venturing, Exploring, and Scoutreach. Programs include council camps, outdoor adventure, STEM and merit badges, character and leadership development, and access support so more Arkansas youth can participate.
geography: Arkansas statewide: Central Arkansas, Northwest Arkansas, River Valley, Arkansas Delta, Ozarks, Ouachitas. Rural and small-town communities plus Little Rock, Fayetteville/Bentonville, Fort Smith, Jonesboro, Pine Bluff, and El Dorado. Do not treat other states as eligible service area.
focusAreas: Camp and facilities (dining halls, water, ADA, cabins, trails, waterfront)
Access for youth from low-income households and Title I schools
lookingFor: Federal, state, foundation, corporate, and civic funding that a 501(c)(3) Scouting council can lead or join as a partner: camp capital and essential community facilities; outdoor recreation; informal STEM; mentoring; character and leadership; camperships and membership financial assistance; AmeriCorps capacity; and pass-through partnerships with schools, cities, counties, and workforce boards.
matchCriteria: Score highly when: 501(c)(3) can apply or partner; Arkansas or nationwide geography; youth development, outdoor/STEM, mentoring, or rural facilities; funds programs, scholarships, or camp infrastructure; reasonable reporting for a council staff team. Flag when a school, city, or university must be lead applicant. Nationwide competitions the council can enter from Arkansas count. Awards locked to another state or a single installation outside Arkansas do not.
poorFit: Never return or score: site-specific awards at a named installation outside Arkansas (including Wright-Patterson AFB / STARBASE Wright Patt or any other single-base STARBASE); state-only programs for Ohio or any state that is not Arkansas; awards that cannot fund Arkansas youth; adult-only workforce; pure biomedical research; invitation-only awards we cannot access; for-profit-only RFPs; and programs that require serving a population the council does not actually enroll.
agencies: Department of Labor WIOA Youth (as partner)
